item.title: Training Framework
item.description:
MARLHF and MADPO share a training framework. Actors generate joint responses, and the task reward ranks them to form preference pairs. The iterative trainers repeat this process against a comparator, while a replay buffer selects the pairs for each update. MARLHF and MADPO describe the two learning objectives.

Collaboration Modes#

collaboration_mode sets the trainable actor layout, and comparator_generation_mode sets the comparator layout in iterative training.

Actor layout Comparator layout Joint responses
Decentralized Decentralized Each role generates its own response on both sides of the comparison.
Decentralized Centralized Separate actors are compared with one comparator that generates all roles’ responses.
Centralized Centralized One actor and one comparator each generate a complete joint response.

The diagram compares the three supported layouts, with the actor on the left and the comparator \( \varpi \) on the right.

item.title: Multi-Agent RLHF
item.description:
Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (MARLHF) fits a joint reward model to preference pairs, then trains the policies with RL using the learned reward. CoMLRL generates the preference labels with the task reward_func.

The training flow is: task items → preference pairs → Stage 1: joint reward learning → Stage 2: policy reinforcement learning. Because the reward model scores the team’s complete response, separate actors learn from one shared reward. MADPO instead optimizes the policies directly from the pairs, without a reward model.

item.title: Multi-Agent DPO
item.description:
Multi-Agent Direct Preference Optimization (MADPO) trains the agents directly from preferred and rejected joint responses, without a reward model or a separate RL stage. Its loss combines all agents’ preference margins, so each policy learns from the team’s outcome.

The training flow is: task items → preference pairs → joint preference loss → policy updates. MARLHF uses the same pairs to fit a joint reward model first and then trains the policies with RL.
